pipeline_result.rationale: Warm plaster and afternoon light establish a warm tone, while the dedicated home-workspace table makes a seated home office the strongest setting match.
pipeline_result.layout: Retain the printer at its initial position, left of center in the lower-middle frame. Build a dedicated rectangular home-workspace table beneath it, independently replacing the gray support. Use an assumed domestic table scale, roughly three printer widths across and twice the printer's base depth, with a warm oak top and simple legs. The printer sits square to the table, with a hand-width of clear surface in front, ample rear clearance and clear margins on both sides. Leave the larger sorting area to its right. The near edge faces an unobstructed standing approach; below it show the table apron, legs and wood floor, not additional tabletop. Place the low sideboard against the rear wall on the right, separated from the table by a usable passage. Product placement permits only one rigid image-plane translation in any view; none is needed here. Furniture is constructed around the unchanged product, not moved as a locked group.
pipeline_result.camera: A medium-wide room view from below standing eye height, looking gently downward with no camera roll. Preserve the printer's existing front, visible top and side surfaces exactly, at their original pixel size and location. Construct the table's long edges rising slightly toward image right and its depth edges receding toward the upper left, square to the printer's chassis in three dimensions. Use a consistent horizon and shared vanishing geometry throughout the room. The near table edge remains accessible, with the entire printer base supported behind it and the sideboard clearly farther away.
pipeline_result.composition: The printer remains fully visible in the middle plane, left of center, on a warm oak workspace table with subtle grain and light wear. Its operating front faces the clear near-camera standing area; no dedicated printer chair is added. The far-right low sideboard has dusty blue painted-wood fronts forming a broad visible band against the rear wall. Keep enough of those fronts visible above and beside the table to make blue noticeable. A single modest stack of plain household and school papers sits on the sideboard's top toward its left end, entirely to the right of the printer silhouette. Render the requested indistinct markings as faint nonlegible marks, not readable added text. Far-left translucent ivory sheers hang at a window and diffuse afternoon light onto warm, lightly textured cream plaster across the rear wall. The near plane contains table legs and uncluttered wood flooring. All requested objects are retained; no other conflict requires omission. Blue is physical paint, never colored lighting or a cast on the printer.

pipeline_result.geometry_text:
BASELINE DIAGRAM MEASUREMENTS from Image 1.
The coordinates, support distances, support top extents, edge locations and support-crop descriptions below describe the initial layout only. They are planning evidence, not required final-scene placement or support geometry. The product's exact view and pixel dimensions remain authoritative.
- Support orientation: the support is turned about 17 degrees to the camera. Its long edges run left to right, rising about 6 degrees toward image right; its short edges recede toward the upper left. The printer's front and sides are parallel to the support edges.
- User-facing edge: the support edge nearest the camera, in front of the printer. At the baseline location it runs from 17% across, 73% down to 86% across, 62% down, about 7% of image height below the printer's lowest point. No support top beyond this edge.
- Product on the support: the printer is 10.0 cm (about 0.3 printer depths) from the user-facing edge. The support top extends 0.19 m (about 0.4 printer widths) toward image left of the printer and 0.69 m (about 1.6 printer widths) toward image right.
- Support size: 1.30 m x 0.65 m, about 3.1 printer widths by 2.1 printer depths.
- Baseline frame crop: 0 of 4 support corners fall outside the frame. For final-scene construction, compose an appropriate support beneath the product at its chosen x-y position. Baseline product-to-edge distances, support top extents, support-edge locations and support cropping may be replaced independently of product translation, provided the base is fully supported and access and perspective remain believable. Never shrink the product to reveal furniture.
- Product baseline: exactly as in Image 1 (details: Image 3), occupying 27-51% across and 50-66% down. Keep this exact product view and pixel size. The listed frame coordinates identify the initial position only; the entire product may undergo one rigid x-y translation while remaining fully inside the frame and unoccluded. This does not allow rotation, resizing, reprojection, cropping or any other product change.
- Camera: 1.37 m high, looking down 13.3 degrees, about 34 mm lens.
